Author: Gautam Kumar Choudhary

Bench: Gautam Kumar Choudhary IN THE HIGH COURT OF JHARKHAND AT RANCHI  Criminal Appeal (S.J.) No. 556 of 2012 [Against the judgment of conviction dated 16.04.2012 and order of sentence dated 17.04.2012 passed by learned Additional Sessions Judge-II, Jamshedpur in Sessions Trial No.322 of 2006]
Deepak Kuma Sah @ Deepak Sao .... .... .... Appellant  --Versus-- The State of Jharkhand .... .... .... Respondent For the Appellants : Mr. Amit Nishant, Amicus Curiae For the State : Mr. Bishambhar Shastri, A.P.P.

sentences.text:

PRESENT : HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE GAUTAM KUMAR CHOUDHARY 1.
The judgment of conviction and sentence under Sections 376(f)/511 of the Indian Penal Code, is under challenge in the instant criminal appeal.
2. The informant of the case is the mother of victim girl aged eight years and was working as maid servant and her husband was serving in the dairy farm.
On the day of incidence, like any other day in the morning, she and her husband had left her home for work 3.

On that day i.e. 21st April, 2006, at 6.30 p.m. when she returned home after days' work, she was informed by her neighbor Panchmukhi Devi that the appellant had carried her daughter towards the bush and attempted to commit rape and on hulla, being raised by her, he fled away.
4. On the written report, Jugsalai (Bagbera) P.S. Case No.85/2006 was registered under Sections 376/511 of the Indian Penal Code.
The police, on investigation, found the case true and submitted charge sheet and the accused was put on trial for the offence under Section 376/511 of the Indian Penal Code.
5. Altogether six witnesses have been examined on the basis of which the judgment of conviction and sentence was pronounced.

6. It is argued by learned Amicus Curiae appearing on behalf of appellant that out of six witnesses,
P.W. 5 and P.W. 6 have not fully supported the case and were declared hostile and the prosecution Deepak Kuma Sah @ Deepak Sao vs The State Of Jharkhand on 15 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/63962620/

sentences.text: 1 case rests on the testimony of P.W. 1- informant, P.W. 2- father, P.W. 3- neighbor and P.W. 4- victim herself.
It is argued that except P.W. 4, none of the witnesses are the direct eye witness to the incidence.
P.W. 3, who was neighbor, has deposed that she saw him while escaping from the place of occurrence, but could not identify him.
The Investigating Officer has not been examined and the medical examination of the victim, was also not conducted.
On these evidences, it is argued that the prosecution has failed to prove its case against the appellant.
7. Learned A.P.P. has defended the judgment of conviction and sentence.
The FIR has been lodged without any delay on the very day of incidence.
The informant has been examined as P.W. 1 and her testimony is corroborated by her written report.
In her cross-examination, she has admitted that she was not a direct eye witness to the incidence.
P.W. 2 is also not eye witness, but he deposed that when he returned to home in the evening, he came to know that an attempt to rape was committed by the appellant.

P.W. 3- Panchmukhi Devi is the neighbor who has deposed that she was at her home when she felt that someone has been muffled and when she raised alarm, she saw one fleeing away from the place of occurrence.
She has not named and identified the appellant, but has fully supported the incidence.
The clinching evidence is of the minor girl P.W. 4, who at the time of her testimony, was ten years of age in 2006.
She has deposed that she had gone to attend her nature call when the appellant attempted to rape her by removing her under pant.
She stood the test of cross- examination and in para 6 has reiterated that she had identified the accused.
8. The medical examination of the victim girl is not imperative necessity particularly when the case was of an attempt to commit rape.
The witnesses have given cogent and trustworthy account of the incidence which does not suffer from the any exaggeration or contradiction.
The law is settled that the testimony of the minor victim girl in sexual assault cases, unsupported by the other witnesses, is sufficient to return the judgment of conviction and sentence.

In the instant case, the testimony of the minor girl, is corroborated by neighbor-P.W. 3 who has supported the incidence, but had no opportunity to see the accused fleeing away from the place of occurrence and I do not find any infirmity in the judgment of conviction.

9. On the point of sentence, considering that no criminal antecedent of the conviction has been brought on record, sentence of four years of R.I. and fine of Rs.5000/- under Sections 376(f)/511 of the Indian Penal Code will meet the ends of justice.
In default of payment of fine, the appellant shall undergo a sentence of three months S.I.
The appeal is dismissed with modification of sentence.

The assistance given by Mr. Amit Nishant, Amicus Curiae is appreciated and Member Secretary,
JHALSA, is directed to pay admissible fees to the amicus curiae.

(Gautam Kumar Choudhary, J.) Jharkhand High Court, Ranchi Dated, 15th February, 2024 NAFR/Anit Deepak Kuma Sah @ Deepak Sao vs The State Of Jharkhand on 15 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/63962620/
